by_judge.judge: D K SINGH & RAJESH RAI K & T.M.NADAF

narrative:
On August 20, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 38.5%, hearing 1,002 of the 2,600 scheduled cases across 57 judges. This represents a moderate contraction in throughput compared to earlier sessions in the week, which registered hearing rates of 42.0% on August 19, 43.3% on August 18, and 41.5% on August 17.

Individual bench productivity reflected substantial variation based on docket size. Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty managed the heaviest individual list with 252 scheduled matters, taking up 85 (33.7%). In Hall 12, Justice R. Nataraj disposed of 65 out of 119 cases (54.6%), while the division bench of Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice T.P. Vivekananda converted 52 of 92 scheduled matters (56.5%). Conversely, heavy single-judge lists experienced lower clearance rates; Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard 12 of 132 cases (9.1%) on his primary roster, and Justice Rajesh Rai K heard 9 of 74 cases (12.2%).

In terms of stage conversion, Orders remained the largest category, comprising 1,032 scheduled matters with 383 heard (37.1%), declining from 45.4% on August 19. Admission matters maintained a 40.2% conversion rate (173 heard of 430), while Preliminary Hearings achieved 42.3% (88 heard of 208). Final Hearings converted 29.4% (153 of 520), reflecting a slight uptick from 22.8% on the prior day.

Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest portion of the docket with 978 scheduled and 350 heard (35.8%). Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) followed with 408 listings and 153 heard (37.5%). Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) saw a lower clearance rate of 36.4% (129 of 354 heard) relative to the 59.5% rate achieved on August 19. Higher clearance efficiencies were observed in Regular Second Appeals (RSA) at 51.6% (80 of 155) and Contempt of Court Cases (CCC) at 52.3% (67 of 128).
